title: Client Reception Routine
summary: How to receive a client from arrival through a calm, prepared start to their visit.
relevance: The Client Reception Routine sets the tone for the entire spa experience. It is the client's first direct interaction with the Zura Spa service standard and should immediately communicate warmth, order, professionalism, attentiveness, and care.

For the team, the routine creates a consistent standard for receiving every client. It ensures that important information is properly gathered, payment and service details are confirmed, and the therapist receives the information needed to prepare appropriately.
For the client, a smooth reception reduces uncertainty and helps them begin relaxing even before they enter the treatment room. The client should feel:
The reception experience should communicate one simple message: "You are welcome, we are prepared for you, and you are in good hands."

guidelines.title: The client should feel
list: Confident in the spa and its team.
Comfortable with what will happen next.

guidelines.title: Appearance
paragraphs: The team member receiving the client must be properly presented before the client arrives.
The client's impression of the spa begins with what they see.
list: Fresh breath and excellent personal hygiene.
No untidy clothing or distracting appearance.
Work area should also be clean and properly arranged.

guidelines.title: Avoid appearing
list: Preoccupied with a phone or another activity.
guidelines.closing: The client should receive your full attention during the reception process.

guidelines.title: Disposition
paragraphs: The warmth should feel natural, not forced or excessive.

procedure.title: Stand and receive the client
procedure.body: As the client enters, rise to your feet. Do not remain seated while receiving a client unless there is a genuine reason you cannot stand. Standing communicates acknowledgement, respect and readiness to attend to the client.

procedure.title: Greet the client warmly
procedure.body: Welcome the client with a genuine smile and professional greeting. Where the client's name is known, use it naturally. Avoid shouting greetings across the room or greeting the client while distracted by another activity.
examples: Good afternoon, Mr. James. Welcome to Zura Spa.

procedure.title: Offer the client a seat
procedure.body: Politely invite the client to sit comfortably. Allow the client a brief moment to settle before immediately beginning questions or discussing payment. The reception should feel organised, not rushed.

procedure.title: Understand the client's needs
procedure.body: Engage the client briefly to understand what they have come for. Do not assume that a returning client automatically wants the same service as their previous visit.
examples: Whether the client already has a booking.
Any existing preference already recorded for a returning client.
Any other information the therapist needs to know.

procedure.title: Present and explain available services
procedure.body: Where the client has not already selected a service, clearly explain the relevant options. Keep the explanation simple, confident, accurate, and helpful. Guide rather than pressure. The objective is to help the client choose the service most suitable for their needs. If you do not know the answer to a client's question, do not guess. Politely confirm the correct information before responding.

procedure.title: Confirm the service and payment
procedure.body: Before proceeding, clearly confirm the selected service, duration, price, any approved add-ons, and payment method. Ensure the client understands what they are paying for before payment is completed. Payment should be properly confirmed before the client proceeds for the session.

procedure.title: Optional relaxation / mind engagement
procedure.body: Where appropriate, the client may be invited to participate in a light and optional mind game or engagement activity. This may be offered before or after payment depending on the situation. Participation must always remain optional. Never pressure a client who does not appear interested.
examples: Help the client settle into the environment.
Make the reception experience more memorable.

procedure.title: Offer water
procedure.body: Water may be offered after payment has been completed, in line with the spa's reception procedure. Where the standard is to provide water upon request, respond promptly and courteously whenever the client requests it. Do not allow the water process to unnecessarily delay the client's session.

procedure.title: Brief the assigned therapist
procedure.body: Before taking the client to the treatment room, communicate all relevant information to the assigned therapist. The therapist should not have to start asking reception for basic information after the client has already entered the room.
examples: Whether the client is new or returning.
Any other relevant information necessary to personalise the session.

procedure.title: Confirm therapist readiness
procedure.body: Notify the assigned therapist that the client is ready. Do not immediately take the client upstairs or into the treatment room. Wait for an affirmative response from the therapist confirming that both the therapist and treatment room are ready. The objective is to prevent the client from entering a room that is still being cleaned, arranged or prepared. The client should never see the team scrambling to get ready for them.

procedure.title: Usher the client to the treatment area
procedure.body: Once the therapist confirms readiness, politely escort the client to the treatment area. Do not simply point toward the staircase or tell a new client to go upstairs. Walk with the client and smoothly hand them over to the assigned therapist. The transition between reception and therapist should feel coordinated and intentional.

notes.title: Things Not to Say or Do During Client Reception
Avoid overly personal comments
paragraphs: Do not make unnecessary remarks about the client's body, weight, shape, skin, clothing, attractiveness, relationship status, or personal life.
Even a compliment can become uncomfortable when it crosses professional boundaries.

notes.title: Do not create doubt about the service
paragraphs: If clarification is needed, obtain the correct information confidently. The client should feel that the team understands the services being offered.
list: I don't really know if this one will work for you.
I've never seen anybody choose this treatment before.
I'm not sure what the therapist normally does.
Maybe you should just try it.

notes.title: Do not make the client feel like an inconvenience
paragraphs: Where there is a genuine delay, communicate professionally and manage the client's expectations without exposing internal disorder.
list: We're trying to arrange the room.
We're almost done with somebody else.

notes.title: Avoid sensitive or divisive conversations
paragraphs: Reception is not the place for unnecessary discussions about politics, religion, ethnic issues, personal relationships, sexual matters, gossip, or other clients.
Allow the client to enjoy a neutral and comfortable environment.

notes.title: Avoid excessive slang and unprofessional humour
paragraphs: Your communication should remain warm without becoming careless.
list: Discussing internal spa problems in front of clients.

notes.title: Do not use your phone while receiving a client
paragraphs: Once a client approaches reception, your attention should shift to the client.

notes.title: Do not discuss other clients
paragraphs: Client confidentiality must be treated as part of the Zura Spa standard.
list: Never reveal who visited the spa.
Never reveal what another client requested.

notes.title: The Reception Standard
paragraphs: A successful reception should move the client smoothly through the following journey: Arrival → Welcome → Comfort → Understanding → Service Confirmation → Payment → Therapist Preparation → Smooth Handover.
At no point should the client feel confused about what is happening next.
By the time the client leaves reception, they should already feel that their relaxation experience has begun.
Every interaction at reception either increases or reduces the client's confidence in Zura Spa. Speak with intention, act with preparation, and make every client feel expected.
